formats.key: submitQuote((uint32 providerId, uint32 productId, uint32 coverAssetId, uint256 coverAmount, uint32 paymentAssetId, uint256 premiumAmount, uint256 feeAmount, uint16 coverExpiry, uint256 validUntil) quote, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)
effects: The signer pays premiumAmount + feeAmount in the payment asset. For an ERC20 this is a transferFrom to the Quote contract, which spends the signer's allowance. For the native coin, msg.value must equal the total.
When the payment asset is an ERC20, any msg.value sent is kept by the contract. It is not added to pendingAmounts, so the operator can collect it.
A soulbound proof-of-cover NFT (quoteId) is minted to the signer. Its owner can claim refunds of the payment if the quote is not settled.
A quote for coverAmount of the cover asset, for coverExpiry, under providerId/productId, is stored and waits for off-chain settlement by the operator.
formats.shown: "Buy cover in <cover asset>", with cover asset, raw cover amount, duration in days, payment asset, raw premium and raw fee. Native value, product and provider are not shown.

findings.title: submitQuote is payable but shows no @.value, and nothing forces it to zero for ERC20 payments.
findings.evidence: QuoteV15.sol _submitQuote: `if (_isNativeCoin(paymentAssetAddress)) { if (msg.value != totalPayment) revert ...} else { safeTransferFrom(...) }`. In the ERC20 branch msg.value is never checked, and it is not added to pendingAmounts, so collect() can sweep it. The descriptor has no `@.value` field.

findings.title: The submitQuote intent names the cover asset but not the payment, so it reads like what you receive, not what you pay.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent "Buy cover in {quote.coverAssetId}". The code takes premiumAmount + feeAmount of paymentAssetId from the signer (_requireValidQuote: `totalPayment = quote.premiumAmount + quote.feeAmount`).
findings.fix: Use "Buy {quote.coverAmount} {quote.coverAssetId} cover for {quote.premiumAmount} + {quote.feeAmount} fee in {quote.paymentAssetId}", or at least name the payment asset.

findings.title: submitQuote shows cover, premium and fee amounts raw, without decimals, because the token is only an ID.
findings.evidence: descriptor fields `#.quote.coverAmount`, `#.quote.premiumAmount`, `#.quote.feeAmount` use format "raw". The token address comes from storage: `_assets[quote.providerId][quote.paymentAssetId].assetAddress` (QuoteV1._requireValidQuote). Decimals differ by asset (ETH 18, USDC 6), so one `unit` decimals value cannot fit.
findings.fix: Nothing in the spec maps a storage asset ID to a token. Per-asset formats would need a token-from-enum feature.

findings.title: The submitQuote assetSymbol enum is static, but asset IDs map to tokens per provider and per chain in storage.
findings.evidence: metadata.enums.assetSymbol {0:ETH,1:DAI,2:USDC,3:USDT,4:POL,5:cbBTC}. The code resolves the ID through `_assets[quote.providerId][quote.paymentAssetId]`, which an admin sets with setAsset. The same enum is used on chains 1, 8453, 10, 137 and 42161.
findings.fix: Confirm that every provider uses these IDs on every chain, or limit deployments to chains where they hold.

findings.title: submitQuote hides productId and providerId, which say what risk the cover protects.
findings.fix: Show the product ID raw, or add an enum of known products.

formats.key: submitQuoteV15((uint32 providerId, uint32 productId, uint32 coverAssetId, uint256 coverAmount, uint32 paymentAssetId, uint256 premiumAmount, uint256 feeAmount, uint16 coverExpiry, uint256 validUntil) quote, address[] coveredAddresses, uint256 integratorId, address mintTo, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)
effects: The signer pays premiumAmount + feeAmount in the payment asset. For an ERC20 this is a transferFrom to the Quote contract, which spends the signer's allowance. For the native coin, msg.value must equal the total.
When the payment asset is an ERC20, any msg.value sent is kept by the contract and is not tracked as a pending payment.
A soulbound proof-of-cover NFT is minted to mintTo, or to the signer if mintTo is zero. That holder gets the refund rights and receives operator refunds.
The cover is recorded for the coveredAddresses list, which may differ from the signer, under providerId/productId, for coverAmount and coverExpiry.
integratorId is stored and only selects the NFT metadata renderer.
formats.shown: "Buy cover in <cover asset>", with cover asset, raw amounts, duration, payment asset and recipient (mintTo). Covered addresses, native value and product are hidden.

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 is payable but shows no @.value, and nothing forces it to zero for ERC20 payments.
findings.evidence: QuoteV15.sol _submitQuote checks msg.value only in the `_isNativeCoin` branch. In the ERC20 branch the ETH stays in the contract, outside pendingAmounts. The descriptor has no `@.value` field.

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 hides coveredAddresses, the wallets the purchased cover actually protects.
findings.evidence: QuoteV15.submitQuoteV15 stores `_quoteCoveredAddresses[quoteId] = coveredAddresses` ("covered addresses which may be different from the sender address"). Descriptor field `#.coveredAddresses` is `visible: never`, and nothing else on the screen states who is insured.
findings.fix: Show `#.coveredAddresses.[]` with format addressName and the label "Covered address".

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 labels mintTo as 'Recipient'; it receives the proof NFT and every refund.
findings.evidence: _submitQuote: `_safeMint(mintTo, quoteId)`. refundQuote sends funds to `ownerOf(quoteId)`, and refundUnfulfilledQuote requires `ownerOf(quoteId) == _msgSender()`. The descriptor label is "Recipient".
findings.fix: Use the label "Cover NFT & refund recipient".

findings.title: The submitQuoteV15 intent names the cover asset but not the payment or its amount.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent "Buy cover in {quote.coverAssetId}". The signer pays premiumAmount + feeAmount of paymentAssetId.

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 shows amounts raw because the token is a storage asset ID.
findings.evidence: fields coverAmount, premiumAmount and feeAmount use format "raw". The asset address comes from `_assets[providerId][paymentAssetId].assetAddress`.

findings.title: The submitQuoteV15 static asset enum may not match the per-provider, per-chain asset IDs in storage.
findings.evidence: metadata.enums.assetSymbol is used for all five chains. The IDs are configured through setAsset per provider.
findings.fix: Verify the mapping for each chain and provider.

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 hides productId and providerId, which define the covered risk.
findings.fix: Show the product ID, or an enum of products.

findings.title: submitQuoteV15 hides coveredAddresses, the wallets the purchased cover actually protects.
findings.reason: On-chain the array is only stored, and it moves none of the signer's assets. The cover position (the NFT) goes to mintTo, which is shown. The quoted text "may be different from the sender address" comes from interface source that is omitted here, and the claim logic that decides what coveredAddresses means for payouts is off-chain. So I cannot tell whether this hides a right or is only the scope of a grant whose holder is shown (not_critical #13).
